claim: Fluorescence microscopy can localize biomolecules inside whole cells and tissues, but its ability to count biomolecules and accuracy of the spatial coordinates is limited by the wavelength of visible light.
source: Fluorescence microscopy can localize biomolecules inside whole cells and tissues, but its ability to count biomolecules and accuracy of the spatial coordinates is limited by the wavelength of visible light.
evidence: This is a statement about the fundamental physical limitations of fluorescence microscopy based on established knowledge of optical physics and microscopy.

claim: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) provides highly accurate position and orientation information of biomolecules but is often confined to small fields of view inside a cell, limiting biological context.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) provides highly accurate position and orientation information of biomolecules but is often confined to small fields of view inside a cell, limiting biological context.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities and limitations of cryo-EM based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: DeCo-LACE was used to collect high-resolution images of entire sections (100- to 250-nm-thick lamellae) of neutrophil-like mouse cells, representing 1–2% of the total cellular volume.
source: In this study, we use a new data-acquisition scheme called Defocus-Corrected Large-Area cryo-EM (DeCo-LACE) to collect high-resolution images of entire sections (100- to 250-nm-thick lamellae) of neutrophil-like mouse cells, representing 1–2% of the total cellular volume.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data collected in the study, including measurements of lamella thickness and calculations of cellular volume represented.

claim: 2D template matching (2DTM) was used to determine localization and orientation of the large ribosomal subunit in cellular sections.
source: We use 2D template matching (2DTM) to determine localization and orientation of the large ribosomal subunit in these sections.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, which is demonstrated through the results showing detected ribosomes.

claim: The data provide maps of ribosomes across entire sections of mammalian cells.
source: These data provide maps of ribosomes across entire sections of mammalian cells.
evidence: This is supported by the figures showing ribosome distributions across lamellae (Figures 4 and 5).

claim: Proteomics using mass-spectrometry is an example of a label-free technique.
source: An example for this is proteomics using mass-spectrometry (Griffin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Griffin et al., 2010.

claim: Cryo-EM has the potential to directly visualize the arrangement of atoms that compose biomolecules inside of cells, thereby allowing label-free detection with high spatial accuracy.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has the potential to directly visualize the arrangement of atoms that compose biomolecules inside of cells, thereby allowing label-free detection with high spatial accuracy.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the capabilities of cryo-EM.

claim: Cryo-EM requires thin samples (<500 nm).
source: Since cryo-EM requires thin samples (<500 nm), imaging of biomolecules inside cells is restricted to small organisms, thin regions of cells, or samples that have been suitably thinned.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the technical requirements of cryo-EM.

claim: Thinning of samples for cryo-EM can be achieved either by mechanical sectioning or by milling using a focused ion beam (FIB).
source: Thinning can be achieved either by mechanical sectioning (McDowall et al., 1983) or by milling using a focused ion beam (FIB) (Villa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to McDowall et al., 1983 and Villa et al., 2013.

claim: The predominant cryo-EM technique for the localization of biomolecules of defined size and shape inside cells is cryo-electron tomography.
source: The predominant cryo-EM technique for the localization of biomolecules of defined size and shape inside cells is cryo-electron tomography (Gan and Jensen, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gan and Jensen, 2012.

claim: The requirement of a tilt series at every imaged location and subsequent image alignment severely limits the throughput for molecular localization in cryo-electron tomography.
source: However, the requirement of a tilt series at every imaged location and subsequent image alignment, severely limits the throughput for molecular localization.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the technical limitations of tomography.

claim: 2D template-matching (2DTM) can identify molecules by their structural fingerprint in single projections.
source: An alternative approach is to identify molecules by their structural fingerprint in single projections using 2D template-matching (2DTM) (Rickgauer et al., 2017; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rickgauer et al., 2017; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: In 2DTM, a 3D model of a biomolecule is used as a template to find 2D projections that match the molecules visible in the electron micrographs.
source: In this method, a 3D model of a biomolecule is used as a template to find 2D projections that match the molecules visible in the electron micrographs.
evidence: This describes the methodology of 2DTM based on established knowledge.

claim: The location of a biomolecule in the z-direction causes predictable aberrations to the projection image, which can be used to calculate complete 3D coordinates and orientations of a biomolecule in a cellular sample.
source: Since the location of a biomolecule in the z-direction causes predictable aberrations to the projection image, this method can be used to calculate complete 3D coordinates and orientations of a biomolecule in a cellular sample (Rickgauer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rickgauer et al., 2020.

claim: The study applied 2DTM of the ribosome large subunit (LSU) to a conditionally immortalized Mus musculus (mouse) cell line that gives rise to functional mature neutrophils.
source: Here we apply 2DTM of the ribosome large subunit (LSU) to a conditionally immortalized Mus musculus (mouse) cell line that gives rise to functional mature neutrophils (Sykes et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study, supported by a citation to Sykes et al., 2016.

claim: Genetic defects in the ribosome machinery often lead to hematopoietic disease.
source: We chose these cells because genetic defects in the ribosome machinery often lead to hematopoietic disease (Kampen et al., 2020) and direct quantification of ribosome location, number and conformational states in hematopoietic cells could lead to new insight into hematopoietic disease (Dolezal et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kampen et al., 2020.

claim: Direct quantification of ribosome location, number and conformational states in hematopoietic cells could lead to new insight into hematopoietic disease.
source: We chose these cells because genetic defects in the ribosome machinery often lead to hematopoietic disease (Kampen et al., 2020) and direct quantification of ribosome location, number and conformational states in hematopoietic cells could lead to new insight into hematopoietic disease (Dolezal et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future insights, supported by a citation to Dolezal et al., 2018.

claim: Aberrations caused by large beam-image shifts and highly condensed beams do not impede LSU detection by 2DTM.
source: 2DTM allows us to test whether aberrations caused by large beam-image shifts and highly condensed beams deteriorate the high-resolution signal. We find that these aberrations do not impede LSU detection by 2DTM.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing consistent detection across different beam-image shift values (Figure 6).

claim: A highly heterogeneous density of ribosomes was found within the cell.
source: We find a highly heterogeneous density of ribosomes within the cell.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing variable ribosome counts across different regions (Figures 4 and 5).

claim: For the foreseeable future computation will be the bottleneck for visual proteomics.
source: Analysis of the throughput in this method suggests that for the foreseeable future computation will be the bottleneck for visual proteomics.
evidence: This is based on inference from the timing data presented in the results section showing that 2DTM computation took approximately one week per lamella.

claim: FIB-milled Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) cells are sufficiently well preserved to permit localization of 60S ribosomal subunits with 2DTM.
source: FIB-milled Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) cells are sufficiently well preserved to permit localization of 60S ribosomal subunits with 2DTM (Lucas et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lucas et al., 2022.

claim: It was unclear whether plunge freezing would be adequate to produce vitreous ice across the whole volume of mammalian cells due to their larger size compared to yeast cells.
source: Due to the larger size of mammalian cells compared to yeast cells, it was unclear whether plunge freezing would be adequate to produce vitreous ice across the whole volume of the cell.
evidence: This is based on inference from established knowledge about the challenges of vitrifying larger samples.

claim: A low magnification image of a representative lamella clearly shows cellular features consistent with a neutrophile-like phenotype, mainly a segmented nucleus and a plethora of membrane-organelles, corresponding to the granules and secretory vesicles of neutrophils.
source: A low magnification image of a representative lamella clearly shows cellular features consistent with a neutrophile-like phenotype, mainly a segmented nucleus and a plethora of membrane-organelles, corresponding to the granules and secretory vesicles of neutrophils (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The resulting micrographs showed smooth bilayered membranes and no signs of crystalline ice, indicating successful vitrification throughout the lamella.
source: The resulting micrographs showed smooth bilayered membranes and no signs of crystalline ice (Figure 1C and D), indicating successful vitrification throughout the lamella.
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: An atomic model of the 60S mouse ribosomal subunit (6SWA) was used for 2DTM.
source: We used an atomic model of the 60S mouse ribosomal subunit (6SWA) for 2DTM (Kraushar et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, supported by a citation to Kraushar et al., 2021.

claim: In a subset of images, the distribution of cross-correlation scores significantly exceeded the distribution expected from images devoid of detectable targets.
source: In a subset of images, the distribution of cross-correlation scores significantly exceeded the distribution expected from images devoid of detectable targets.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data from 2DTM analysis.

claim: In the resulting scaled maximum-intensity projections (MIPs), clear peaks with SNR values up to 10 were apparent.
source: In the resulting scaled maximum-intensity projections (MIPs), clear peaks with SNR values up to 10 were apparent (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In images of cytosolic compartments there were 10–500 ribosomes within one micrograph.
source: Using a threshold criterion to select significant targets (see Methods), we found that in images of cytosolic compartments there were 10–500 ribosomes within one micrograph (Figure 1B–E).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 1B-E.

claim: No targets were found in areas corresponding to the nucleus or mitochondria.
source: Notably, we found no targets in areas corresponding to the nucleus (Figure 1B) or mitochondria (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 1B and 1D.

claim: In the cytoplasm, a highly variable number of targets was found, only ~50 in some exposures and up to 500 in others.
source: In the cytoplasm, we found a highly variable number of targets, only ~50 in some exposures (Figure 1E) and up to 500 in others (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 1C and 1E.

claim: DeCo-LACE uses three key strategies: (1) every electron that exposes a fresh area of the sample is collected on the camera, (2) image shift is used to precisely and quickly raster the surface of a lamella, and (3) focusing is done without using a sacrificial area.
source: This approach uses three key strategies: (1) every electron that exposes a fresh area of the sample is collected on the camera, (2) image shift is used to precisely and quickly raster the surface of a lamella, and (3) focusing is done without using a sacrificial area (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in the study, illustrated in Figures 2A and B.

claim: The electron beam size was adjusted to be entirely contained by the detector area to ensure that every electron exposing a fresh area of the sample is captured by the detector.
source: To ensure that every electron exposing a fresh area of the sample is captured by the detector, we adjusted the electron beam size to be entirely contained by the detector area.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: During canonical low-dose imaging, the microscope is configured so that the focal plane is identical to the eucentric plane of the specimen stage, which leaves the C2 aperture out of focus, resulting in ripples at the edge of the beam.
source: During canonical low-dose imaging, the microscope is configured so that the focal plane is identical to the eucentric plane of the specimen stage. This leaves the C2 aperture out of focus, resulting in ripples at the edge of the beam (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about microscope optics, illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: Data was collected on eight lamellae, four using the eucentric focus condition and four using the fringe-free condition.
source: We used this strategy to collect data on eight lamellae, four using the eucentric focus condition, hereafter referred to as LamellaEUC, and four using the fringe-free condition, hereafter referred to as LamellaFFF (Figure 3A-F, Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This describes the experimental data collected in the study.

claim: Data were collected with a highly consistent defocus of 800 nm in both the eucentric focus and fringe-free focus conditions.
source: We were able to collect data with a highly consistent defocus of 800 nm (Figure 2F), both in the eucentric focus and fringe-free focus condition.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The defocus was consistent across a lamella, except for rare outliers and in images containing contamination.
source: To ensure that data were collected consistently, we mapped defocus values as a function of the applied image shift (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A). This demonstrated that the defocus was consistent across a lamella, except for rare outliers and in images containing contamination.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The measured objective astigmatism of each lamella varies with the applied image shift, becoming more astigmatic mostly due to image shift in the x direction.
source: We also plotted the measured objective astigmatism of each lamella and found that it varies with the applied image shift, becoming more astigmatic mostly due to image shift in the x direction (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In the resulting montages, the same cellular features visible in the overview images are apparent.
source: In the resulting montages, the same cellular features visible in the overview images are apparent (Figure 3B+E, Figure 3—figure supplement 4B), however due to the high magnification and low defocus many more details, such as the membrane bilayer separation, can be observed (Figure 3C+F).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 3B, 3E, 3C, 3F, and Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: For montages collected using the eucentric condition, there are clearly visible fringes at the edges between the tiles, which are absent in the fringe-free focus montages.
source: For montages collected using the eucentric condition, there are clearly visible fringes at the edges between the tiles (Figure 3C), which are absent in the fringe-free focus montages (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 3C and 3F.

claim: The fringes do not impede target detection by 2DTM, making them primarily an aesthetic issue.
source: In our analysis below, we show that these fringes do not impede target detection by 2DTM, making them primarily an aesthetic issue.
evidence: This is based on inference from the analysis showing similar detection rates in both conditions.

claim: The tiling pattern is visible in the montages, which is believed to be due to the non-linear behavior of the K3 camera.
source: We also note that the tiling pattern is visible in the montages (Figure 3B+E), which we believe is due to the non-linear behavior of the K3 camera since we can observe these shading artifacts in images of a condensed beam over vacuum (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on inference from observations of shading artifacts in control images (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).

claim: A substantial number of granules seemed to contain a membrane-enclosed inclusion with density similar to the surrounding cytosol.
source: We found that a substantial number of granules, which are characterized by higher density inside the surrounding cytosol (Bainton et al., 1971), seemed to contain a membrane-enclosed inclusion with density similar to the surrounding cytosol (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C) and could therefore be formed by inward budding of the granule membrane.
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C and a citation to Bainton et al., 1971.

claim: The granules with inclusions were 150–300 nm in diameter and the inclusions were 100–200 nm in diameter.
source: These granules were 150–300 nm in diameter and the inclusions were 100–200 nm in diameter.
evidence: This is supported by measurements from the image data.

claim: Based on the dimensions, the granules are either azurophil or specific granules.
source: Based on these dimensions the granules are either azurophil or specific granules (Bainton et al., 1971).
evidence: This is based on inference from the measured dimensions and a citation to Bainton et al., 1971.

claim: These inclusions have not been described in granulocytes to the authors' knowledge.
source: To our knowledge, these inclusions have not been described in granulocytes and are further described and discussed below.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the observation based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: In initial attempts of using 2DTM on micrographs acquired with the DeCo-LACE protocol, no SNR peaks above threshold were observed using the large subunit of the mouse ribosome.
source: In our initial attempts of using 2DTM on micrographs acquired with the DeCo-LACE protocol, we did not observe any SNR peaks above threshold using the large subunit of the mouse ribosome (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the initial experimental results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The edges of the beam might interfere with motion-correction of the movies as they represent strong low-resolution features that do not move with the sample.
source: We reasoned that the edges of the beam might interfere with motion-correction of the movies as they represent strong low-resolution features that do not move with the sample.
evidence: This is based on inference about the potential cause of the initial failure to detect targets.

claim: When the movie frames were cropped to exclude the beam edges, the estimated amount of motion increased, consistent with successful tracking of sample motion.
source: When we cropped the movie frames to exclude the beam edges, the estimated amount of motion increased (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with successful tracking of sample motion.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In the motion-corrected average after cropping, significant SNR peaks could be identified, confirming the high sensitivity of 2DTM to the presence of high-resolution signal preserved in the images by the motion correction.
source: Furthermore, in the motion-corrected average we could identify significant SNR peaks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), confirming the high sensitivity of 2DTM to the presence of high-resolution signal preserved in the images by the motion correction.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Consistently total motion below 1 Å per frame was found across all tiles in the eight lamellae.
source: Using this approach, we motion-corrected all tiles in the eight lamellae and found consistently total motion below 1 Å per frame (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In some lamellae, increased motion was found in the lamella center, which indicates areas of variable mechanical stability within FIB-milled lamellae.
source: In some lamellae, we found increased motion in the lamella center, which indicates areas of variable mechanical stability within FIB-milled lamellae.
evidence: This is based on inference from the motion data.

claim: The beam edges gave rise to artifacts in the MIP and numerous false-positive detections at the edge of the illuminated area in some micrographs.
source: In some micrographs, we also observed that the beam edges gave rise to artifacts in the MIP and numerous false-positive detections at the edge of the illuminated area (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Overlaying the positions of detected LSUs on the lamella montages reveals the LSU distribution throughout the FIB-milled slices of individual cells.
source: We used the tile positions to calculate the positions of the detected LSUs in the lamellae (Figure 4A, Figure 5A, Figure 4—video 1, Figure 5—video 1). Overlaying these positions of the lamella montages reveals the LSU distribution throughout the FIB-milled slices of individual cells.
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 4A, 5A, and associated videos.

claim: Consistent with prior observations imaging selected views in yeast, organelles like the nucleus and mitochondria only showed sporadic targets detected with low SNRs, consistent with the estimated false-positive rate of one per tile.
source: Consistent with prior observations imaging selected views in yeast (Lucas et al., 2022), organelles like the nucleus and mitochondria only showed sporadic targets detected with low SNRs, consistent with the estimated false-positive rate of one per tile.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and a citation to Lucas et al., 2022.

claim: The side views indicated that lamellae were thinner at the leading edge.
source: Furthermore, the side views indicated that lamellae were thinner at the leading edge.
evidence: This is based on inference from the side view images showing ribosome positions.

claim: The thickness of the lamellae varied between 100 and 250 nm, with consistently thinner ice at the leading edge even though the lamellae were prepared with the overtilt approach.
source: To confirm this we estimated the ice thickness in individual tiles using the Beer-Lambert law (Rice et al., 2018) with 322 nm as coefficient (Rice et al., 2018; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B). We found that the thickness of the lamellae varied between 100 and 250 nm, with consistently thinner ice at the leading edge even though we prepared the lamellae with the overtilt approach (Schaffer et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and citations to Rice et al., 2018 and Schaffer et al., 2017.

claim: For most tiles, the apparent thickness of LSU detections was at least 70 nm less than the estimated sample thickness, indicating that no detections were being made within 35 nm of the lamella edge.
source: To further confirm the relationship of the range in Z-positions of detections and sample thickness we plotted the range in Z-positions as a function of the estimated sample thickness (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C). For most tiles, the apparent thickness of LSU detections was at least 70 nm less than the estimated sample thickness, indicating that no detections were being made within 35 nm of the lamella edge.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: It is possible that the lack of detections near the lamella edge is caused by sample damage during FIB-milling as similar values for damaged areas in FIB-milled lamellae have been estimated from sub-tomogram averaging.
source: It is possible that this is caused by sample damage during FIB-milling as similar values for damaged areas in FIB-milled lamellae have been estimated from sub-tomogram averaging (Berger et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to Berger et al., 2022.

claim: LSU detections across the lamellae can be skewed by a change in thickness and sample damage.
source: This means that LSU detections across the lamellae can be skewed by a change in thickness and sample damage.
evidence: This is based on inference from the observations about thickness variation and potential damage.

claim: Better sample preparation methods together with a better understanding of the damage to the sample during FIB-milling are needed to accurately quantify molecular concentrations.
source: Therefore, better sample preparation methods together with a better understanding of the damage to the sample during FIB-milling are needed to accurately quantify molecular concentrations.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on inference from the observed limitations.

claim: LSUs could be seen associating with membranes, in patterns reminiscent of the rough endoplasmic reticulum or the outer nuclear membrane.
source: Close inspection of the LSU positions in the lamellae revealed several interesting features. LSUs could be seen associating with membranes, in patterns reminiscent of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (Figure 4C, Figure 5C) or the outer nuclear membrane (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 4C, 4D, and 5C.

claim: LSUs were observed forming ring-like structures, potentially indicating circularized mRNAs.
source: We also observed LSUs forming ring-like structures (Figure 4E), potentially indicating circularized mRNAs (Wells et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the image data shown in Figure 4E, supported by a citation to Wells et al., 1998.

claim: While ribosomes were for the most part excluded from the numerous granules observed in the cytoplasm, in some cases clusters of LSUs were observed in the inclusions of double-membraned granules.
source: While ribosomes were for the most part excluded from the numerous granules observed in the cytoplasm, in some cases we observed clusters of LSUs in the inclusions of double-membraned granules described earlier (Figure 4F, Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the image data shown in Figures 4F, 5D, and 5E.

claim: In the case of Figure 5E, the detected LSUs span the whole lamella in the z direction, which is consistent with the hypothesis that the inclusions are of cytoplasmic origin.
source: However, in the case of Figure 5E, the detected LSUs span the whole lamella in the z direction (Figure 5F), while positions above or below a granule would result in LSUs situated exclusively at the top or bottom of the lamella. This is consistent with the earlier hypothesis that the inclusions are of cytoplasmic origin.
evidence: This is based on inference from the z-position data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Different numbers of detected targets were found within the eight lamellae, ranging from 1089–6,433 per lamella.
source: Within the eight lamellae we found different numbers of detected targets, ranging from 1089–6,433 per lamella (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: LamellaEUC 1 had the most detected targets, but also had the largest surface area and contained cytoplasm from two cells.
source: LamellaEUC 1 had the most detected targets, but also had the largest surface area and contained cytoplasm from two cells.
evidence: This is based on observations from the image data.

claim: LamellaFFF 4 had the fewest detected targets, but this particular lamella was dominated by a circular section of the nucleus, with only small pockets of cytoplasm.
source: LamellaFFF 4 had the fewest detected targets, but this particular lamella was dominated by a circular section of the nucleus, with only small pockets of cytoplasm (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on observations from the image data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: When comparing the distribution of scores between lamellae, they were found to be fairly comparable with median SNRs ranging from 8.7 to 9.7.
source: When comparing the distribution of scores between lamellae, we found them to be fairly comparable with median SNRs ranging from 8.7 to 9.7 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: LamellaEUC 1 had slightly lower scores compared to the rest, potentially due to its large size and connected mechanical instability during imaging.
source: LamellaEUC 1 had slightly lower scores compared to the rest, potentially due to its large size and connected mechanical instability during imaging.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on inference from the data.

claim: No differences were observed in the number or SNR of detected targets between eucentric or fringe-free illumination conditions that were bigger than the observed inter-lamella variability.
source: Overall, we did not observe differences in the number or SNR of detected targets between eucentric or fringe-free illumination conditions that were bigger than the observed inter-lamella variability.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the data across different conditions.

claim: Uniformly high SNR values were found throughout the illuminated areas for both eucentric and fringe-free focus illumination, demonstrating that both illumination schemes are suitable for DeCo-LACE.
source: When plotting the SNR values of detected targets in all eight lamellae as a function of their location in the tiles, we found uniformly high SNR values throughout the illuminated areas for both eucentric and fringe-free focus illumination, demonstrating that both illumination schemes are suitable for DeCo-LACE (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In both eucentric and fringe-free focus conditions more targets were detected at the back edge of the lamella.
source: Instead, we observed that in both eucentric and fringe-free focus conditions more targets were detected at the back edge of the lamella (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The increase in matches at the back of the lamellae compared to the front may be due to the center of the cell being predominantly occupied by the nucleus, despite its segmentation in neutrophil-like cells.
source: This may be due to the center of the cell being predominantly occupied by the nucleus, despite its segmentation in neutrophil-like cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on inference from the data.

claim: The increase in matches at the back of the lamellae compared to the front can also be explained by the thickness gradient of the lamellae.
source: The increase in matches at the back of the lamellae compared to the front can also be explained by the thickness gradient of the lamellae (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, Figure 4B, Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on inference from the thickness data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: SNRs were on average the highest at the front edge of the lamellae, presumably due to the reduced sample thickness.
source: In addition, aberrations would be expected to cause average 2DTM SNRs to be higher when beam-image shift values are small. Instead, we found that SNRs where on average the highest at the front edge of the lamellae (Figure 6F), presumably due to the reduced sample thickness.
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 6F and inference about the cause.

claim: Factors other than beam image-shift or beam condensation aberrations are limiting 2DTM SNRs, predominantly the thickness of the lamellae.
source: We therefore conclude that factors other that beam image-shift or beam condensation aberrations are limiting 2DTM SNRS, predominantly the thickness of the lamellae.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on inference from the data analysis.

claim: All lamellae described were derived from a clonal cell line under identical condition and thinned with the same parameters.
source: All lamellae described above were derived from a clonal cell line under identical condition and thinned with the same parameters.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: The substantial variability of detected targets between the lamellae must be due to sample preparation variability, including area, thickness, mechanical stability, and location of the section within the cell.
source: This means that the substantial variability of detected targets between the lamellae must be due to sample preparation variability, including area, thickness, mechanical stability, and location of the section within the cell.
evidence: This is based on inference from the observation of variability despite controlled conditions.

claim: Further studies that want to draw quantitative and statistically relevant conclusions about the number and location of molecules under different experimental conditions will require collection of orders of magnitude more data than in this study to gain enough statistical power given the observed variability.
source: We therefore predict that further studies that want to draw quantitative and statistically relevant conclusions about the number and location of molecules under different experimental conditions, will require collection of orders of magnitude more data than in this study to gain enough statistical power given this variability.
evidence: This is a prediction based on inference from the observed variability.

claim: The samples used were prepared in two 24 hr sessions on a FIB/SEM instrument, and imaging was performed during another two 24 hr session on the TEM microscope.
source: The samples used were prepared in two 24 hr sessions on a FIB/SEM instrument, and imaging was performed during another two 24 hr session on the TEM microscope.
evidence: This describes the experimental timeline.

claim: The milling time per lamella was ~30 min and TEM imaging was accomplished in ~10 s per tile or 90 min for a~6 × 6 μm lamella.
source: Inspections of the timestamps of the raw data files revealed that the milling time per lamella was ~30 min and TEM imaging was accomplished in ~10 s per tile or 90 min for a~6 × 6 μm lamella.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the experimental data timestamps.

claim: Processing of the data took substantially longer than sample preparation and imaging.
source: Processing of the data, however, took substantially longer.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the processing time to the experimental time.

claim: 2DTM of all tiles took approximately one week per lamella on 32 Nvidia A6000 GPUs.
source: Specifically, 2DTM of all tiles took approximately one week per lamella on 32 Nvidia A6000 GPUs.
evidence: This describes the computational resources and time required.

claim: Computation is a bottleneck in the current workflow.
source: Computation is therefore a bottleneck in our current workflow, and further optimizations of the algorithm may be necessary to increase throughput.

claim: The two main advantages of the developed approach compared to previous approaches are high throughput of imaging and biological context for detected molecules.

claim: Granules containing a vesicle of putative cytosolic origin were observed.
source: We observed granules containing a vesicle of putative cytosolic origin.

claim: Upon degranulation, the process in which granules fuse with the plasma membrane, these vesicles would be released into the extracellular space.
source: We speculate that upon degranulation, the process in which granules fuse with the plasma membrane, these vesicles would be released into the extracelullar space.

source: The main types of extracellular vesicles of this size are exosomes, up to 100 nm large vesicles derived from fusion of multivesicular bodies with the plasma membrane, and microvesicles, which are derived from direct budding of the plasma membrane (van Niel et al., 2018).

claim: Granulocytes could release a third type of extracellular vesicle, granule-derived vesicles (GDV), into the extracellular space.

claim: 2DTM showed that a subset of GDVs can contain ribosomes.
source: 2DTM showed that a subset of GDVs can contain ribosomes (Figure 4F, Figure 5D and E).

claim: A consistent shading artifact pattern was found in the montages, which is believed to be the result of non-linear behavior of the K3 camera.
source: As mentioned in the results, we found a consistent shading artifact pattern in our montages, that we believe is the result of non-linear behavior of the K3 camera.
evidence: This is based on inference from observations of the artifact pattern.

claim: When averaging images with a condensed beam taken over vacuum, a consistent background pattern with a brighter region on the periphery of the illuminated area was found in both focus conditions.
source: Indeed, when we average images with a condensed beam taken over vacuum we found in both focus conditions a consistent background pattern with a brighter region on the periphery of the illuminated area (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The shading pattern might be caused by dynamic adjustment of the internal camera counting threshold which expects columns of the sensor to be evenly illuminated as is the case for SPA applications.
source: This might be caused by dynamic adjustment of the internal camera counting threshold which expects columns of the sensor to be evenly illuminated as is the case for SPA applications.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed artifact.

claim: Since the signal of the shading pattern has mainly low-resolution components it is unlikely to affect 2DTM.
source: Since the signal of this pattern has mainly low-resolution components it is unlikely to affect 2DTM.
evidence: This is based on inference about the impact of the artifact on the analysis.

claim: The non-linear behavior of the camera has to be taken into account when imaging samples with strongly varying density and unusual illumination schemes.

claim: Even though beam image-shift was used extensively (up to 7 µm), substantially reduced 2DTM SNR values were not seen in tiles acquired at high beam image-shift compared to tiles acquired with low or no beam image-shift.
source: We found that even though we used beam image-shift extensively (up to 7 µm), we did not see substantially reduced 2DTM SNR values in tiles acquired at high beam image-shift compared to tiles acquired with low or no beam image-shift.
evidence: This is supported by the data analysis comparing SNR values across different beam-image shift values.

claim: This finding is unexpected because beam image-shift is thought to degrade the high-resolution signal due to the introduction of beam-tilt, as has been observed in single particle analysis.
source: This is unexpected because beam image-shift is thought to degrade the high-resolution signal due to the introduction of beam-tilt, as has been observed in single particle analysis (Cash et al., 2020; Cheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge supported by citations to Cash et al., 2020 and Cheng et al., 2018.

claim: The structure of the mouse LSU used was deposited into the PDB with atoms having a median B-factor of ~80 Å2, which was multiplied by 1.5 before generating the density map.
source: In our case, we used a structure of the mouse LSU that was deposited into the PDB with atoms having a median B-factor of ~80 Å2, which we multiplied by 1.5 before generating the density map.

source: This value was chosen empirically early in the study to optimize the number of detections.

claim: The resulting median B-factor of 120 Å2 is equivalent to a Gaussian lowpass filter with a filter constant of 7.7 Å.
source: The resulting median B-factor of 120 Å2 is equivalent to a Gaussian lowpass filter with a filter constant of 7.7 Å.

source: At this beam-tilt we expect a phase error of larger than π/4 at resolutions higher than 5.75 Å (Cheng et al., 2018), which exceeds the effective resolution of our 2DTM template.
evidence: This is based on calculation and a citation to Cheng et al., 2018.

claim: The beam-tilt caused by beam-image shift did not strongly affect detections in the present study, but it might be important to consider when imaging at even higher beam-image shift values or when using higher resolution signal in 2DTM.

claim: Simulations of 2DTM suggest that it should be possible to detect protein molecules as small as 300 kDa in a crowded environment.

claim: The conformational homogeneity of a protein complex is expected to affect the ability to detect it.
